title: 5 Things you need to know about A Car Extended Warranty
summary: A dealership insider ('Chevy Dude') explains the two basic types of extended warranty (exclusionary vs. stated coverage), debunks 'bumper-to-bumper' and 'lifetime' marketing terms, and covers pricing and deductibles.

assertions.quote: there is what's called an exclusionary warranty and there's one called stated coverage

verdicts.note: Matches standard vehicle service contract industry terminology.

assertions.quote: if it is not listed then it's covered

verdicts.note: Follows from how exclusionary contracts are structured, though actual breadth still depends on the specific exclusion list.

assertions.quote: they're junk number one you'll never make a claim on them

verdicts.note: Some 'lifetime' warranties have narrow qualifying conditions that reduce payout rates, but 'never' is an overstatement from one insider's opinion.

assertions.quote: certified pre-owned is a stated coverage

verdicts.note: Consistent with how CPO warranty programs are typically structured, though terms vary by manufacturer.
True of a signed contract price in general, though it ignores the time value of money and the chance the vehicle is sold before it matters.

assertions.quote: you know exactly what your repair costs are going to cost you over the term of your extended warranty

verdicts.note: Only true for repairs that are ultimately approved; claim denials and exclusions mean actual out-of-pocket costs aren't fully capped in practice.

assertions.quote: if a part comes in and it's 300 that means the extended warranty company is only paying 100

verdicts.note: Describes a real parts-cost-cap mechanism some contracts use, but not all contracts cap payout this way.

assertions.quote: that piece of paper that your extended warranty is written on is worth absolutely nothing
